rationale: Round 1 compiled, ran correctly, and needed no ICE fallback, so this round pushes obfuscation intensity up across the board while keeping the risk gates that protect correctness. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain because misr's core is the large simulate/main control flow, where flattening destroys the region structure an analyst relies on; BCF and IBR follow closely to add opaque predicates and indirect branching on those same hot functions, with RuntimeCost held near 0.5 so the weight still discriminates against stacking all three on the innermost simulate loop. IGV and ICALL are boosted to obscure the small program's simple global-state and direct-call graph, which is its main remaining attack surface given only 6 functions. SPLIT keeps high DiversityGain but the highest RuntimeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights so it is applied mainly to the larger functions (simulate, main) rather than the tiny create_link_list/kill_list where splitting adds little and risks breakage. SUB stays moderate since arithmetic substitution on a mostly-branching benchmark yields limited gain and its low size cost is the only scarce resource worth spending elsewhere. Overall the table trades size headroom (total text is only 1805 bytes, so SizeCost weights stay permissive) for stronger control-flow obfuscation, while RuntimeCost and CorrectnessRisk weights remain high enough to keep simulate's runtime overhead acceptable and preserve the correct behavior confirmed in round 1.
